government.note: Parliamentary republic; in 2000 the country was the Republic of Macedonia (admitted to the UN as 'the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia') and was renamed North Macedonia in 2019 after the Prespa Agreement with Greece. The President is directly elected for five years (two terms at most) in two rounds; before the 2009 constitutional amendment the second round also needed a 50% turnout, and now a 40% turnout. The Government is headed by the Prime Minister and responsible to the unicameral Assembly (Sobranie). Referendums are valid only with a turnout above 50%.

system.note: Since 2002: six constituencies electing 20 members each by proportional representation; three diaspora seats were added for the 2011 and 2014 elections (123 members). The 1998 Assembly was elected by a mixed system (85 single-member constituencies in two rounds and 35 national list seats). seats_2000 is the result of the October-November 1998 election; changes before 1 January 2000 were not checked. The PDP and DPA ran a joint national list in 1998; their constituency seats are shown separately.
